decisions.reason: The piqué upholstery fabric sits squarely in the firm's core upholstery knowledge and has its own page, so in-house development can keep interpreting feedback and refining it rather than dropping it.
The bouclé-effect sheer draws on established decoration expertise the firm can assimilate well, but its low visibility after two years raises the risk of it being rotated out of the collection.
Flame-retardant jacquard curtains combine the firm's functional-fabric know-how with contract and hospitality demand, making the product a strong platform for continued learning and improvement.

The double-face wool blend extends existing capabilities and supports the renewable-materials push, though its blend composition and limited prominence leave it exposed as hard-to-recycle blends are reduced.
The wool bouclé leno builds on sheer-fabric and wool knowledge and fits the sustainability direction, so the firm can absorb market feedback and develop it further despite its modest visibility.

The newly launched braided upholstery and curtain fabric builds on established weaving know-how, has its own page, and is too early in its life for the firm to have learned enough to justify dropping it.
